elements.element: No MFN / most-favoured-nation pricing obligation is imposed on Customer
elements.evidence: Operation 1: delete_paragraph p0026 removes "Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives."

elements.element: No obligation on Customer to disclose more favourable third-party offers to Vendor
elements.evidence: The disclosure duty ("must disclose ... any more favourable commercial offer it receives") is deleted in its entirety.

elements.element: No obligation on Customer to match / give Vendor a right to match before engaging another provider
elements.evidence: "Before engaging another provider, Customer must ... match for Vendor" is deleted.

elements.element: MFN pricing running in Customer's favour remains permissible (not prohibited)
elements.evidence: Deletion only; nothing added that bars Customer-favourable MFN pricing.

elements.element: Any MFN obligation is limited to a defined product
elements.evidence: No MFN clause remains after the deletion, so no defined-product limitation exists (the fallback bargain is not the level implemented).

elements.element: Any MFN obligation is limited to a 12-month term
elements.evidence: No surviving MFN language and no 12-month duration.

elements.element: Reasonable-comparison carve-outs apply to the MFN
elements.evidence: No carve-out language present; clause removed entirely.

reasons: The locked preferred level ('No MFN obligation on Customer') is fully achieved: the single sentence in § 7.2 contained only the disclose-and-match MFN duty, and it is removed with no substitute language.

The deterministic minimality gate objects to a whole-paragraph deletion, but § 7.2 consists exclusively of the offending obligation — there is no non-offending operative text left to preserve, so no narrower operator, number, or phrase edit could reach the preferred position. On the substance the edit is minimal: one delete, zero added words.

Intent preserved: nothing else in § 7.2 is disturbed, no defined term is orphaned, and the edit is consistent with § 12.3's confirmation that Customer has made no most-favoured-customer commitment (removing a latent contradiction rather than creating one).

Fallback elements (defined product, 12 months, reasonable-comparison carve-outs) are unmet, but that is expected and acceptable because the preferred level is a separate, stronger bargain and is satisfied.
Margin comment is non-operative and correctly explains the change without adding obligations.
